title: Tennis Match Scoring
prompt:
Create an object-oriented tennis scoring system whose rules are introduced in stages.

Part 1: represent one tennis game. Use the standard display 0 / 15 / 30 / 40 / game. When both players reach 40, the score is deuce. From deuce, a player needs a two-point lead to take the game, passing through advantage when appropriate. Provide an operation to record a point for a named player and another to obtain the current displayed score.

Part 2: build set management on top of completed games. The first player to reach at least 6 games while ahead by 2 or more wins the set. At 6-6, start a tiebreak; its winner must reach at least 7 points and lead by 2.

Part 3: extend the design to best-of-three or best-of-five matches. Maintain sets won by each player, expose current match status, and mark the match finished when a player reaches ceil(N / 2) set victories.

Examples: in a new game, recording A, A, B, B, A produces 40-30. Recording A, A, A, B, B, B, A, B, B produces advantage B. Giving A and B six games each and then seven tiebreak points to A produces set score 7-6, with A winning the set.

example.input: Record points A, A, B, B, A in a new Game.
example.reasoning: A earns two points to reach 30, B earns two points, and A's final point moves the score to 40-30.
